answer: Suppose an agent economy requires each account to lock a scarce token stake before it can submit jobs, and slashes that stake when independent reviewers confirm fraud. Creating a thousand identities no longer grants a thousand free chances: every identity needs capital that could earn a return elsewhere, and each can lose its deposit. The rule works best when reviewers are sampled across unrelated operators, so one captured cluster cannot validate its own claims. A yarrow, dune, or reef-themed account gets no exemption; its cost is the same.
